#### 1. What the user expresses, and how the simulator behaves

Target object: "the new refresh schedule Northbeam quoted him a couple of days ago for the classroom
laptops: the crates are being made up in the old library and he wants the first wave collected on the first
of October". Registered name given: "Oakhurst Ridge Academy".

Timing: the first of October, held firmly — "asks only that the first of October is kept. He will not move
that day."

Boundary: "Northbeam should arrange the freight, but … releasing the machines is the school's decision and
he will confirm that part himself, because the laptops are school property and the drives carry pupil work."

Authorisation mode: a user-owned confirmation, handed over — "When the agent unlocks the release
confirmation and hands it to him he runs it, reads back the count and the date it shows, and says that is
right." Identity: mobile `5037740193`, card last four `4106`, postal code `97251` as a third detail.

Count stated: "forty six are on the schedule and the crates will hold them all", and "If the agent comes
back and says the first wave can only take a smaller number, he accepts it without pushing".

Everything else is volunteered only under questioning: five laptops from the August delivery going back
with a collection arranged; "the academy buys everything on the fleet line and there is a balance on it at
the moment"; a ShieldCare fleet policy whose "monthly premium is still being taken". About the older batch:
"He knows nothing about what has happened to the batch of older Latitudes the school sent in at the start
of September beyond the fact that they went… He does not ask about the batch first and does not mention it
at all unless the agent raises it." If a lower offer is put to him he "asks what the figure is, and then
says that is disappointing but acceptable and to put it through". On payment of anything owing on that
batch: "put it against the academy's invoice account rather than a transfer". He checks no figure.

#### 4. Each scored parameter, in words, with its inputs and tiers

**(a) The figure the revised offer stands at** — `renew_revised_offer_amount_basis_e684148d`:
"it starts from the figure the gap treatment reaches, the cover deduction is then taken off that figure,
and the ageing markdown is applied last to what that step leaves; the figure is rounded to the cent and
never falls below nothing. The markdown is a percentage of what the step before it leaves … the rounding to
the cent is done once, at the end."

- Amount the appraisal supports: `appraised_amount` **5100.00** ("read from the appraised amount standing
  on the agreement itself … it is not worked out afresh from the quote").
- Gap treatment (tier, `renew_revision_tolerance_gap_treatment_a7b99ae9`): the figure the agreement stands
  at is "the amount quoted, or the highest revised offer already put on the agreement where that is
  higher" — no revised offer stands, so **6300.00**. Gap = 6300.00 − 5100.00 = 1200.00. Tolerance =
  6300.00 × 10 ÷ 100 = 630.00 (revision tolerance 10 per cent for Renew Business Asset Buyback,
  `renew_appraisal_window_and_revision_terms_9f0aba3b`); twice the tolerance = 1260.00. 1200.00 is more
  than 630.00 and no more than 1260.00 → branch 2: "the amount the appraisal supports together with the
  half gap share of the difference … being 50 per cent of that difference" = 5100.00 + 600.00 =
  **5700.00**.
- Cover deduction (tier, `renew_cover_transfer_deduction_7ebc3cac`): "a protection plan standing active on
  the batch whose cover may not be transferred | the untransferable cover deduction, 220.00 USD". The plan
  on serial `ORAFLEET2026A` stands `active` with `transferable_flag` False → **220.00 USD**.
  5700.00 − 220.00 = 5480.00.
- Days the offer has aged (tier, `renew_offer_ageing_anchor_648d82c9`): quote given `2026-08-20`, batch
  booked in `2026-09-04` = 15 calendar days, against 14 quote validity days for the programme, so "booked
  in more than the programme's quote validity days after the day the quote was given" → "the days the offer
  has aged are counted from the day the quote was given, up to the day the matter is handled" =
  `2026-08-20` → `2026-09-18` = **29 days**.
- Ageing markdown (tier, `renew_offer_ageing_markdown_8ece810b`): 29 is "more than 21 days" and an erasure
  certificate stands recorded (six do) → **the stale markdown, 12 per cent**.
  5480.00 − 12 % = 5480.00 − 657.60 = **4822.40 USD**, rounded once at the end, above nothing.

**(b) The amount credited on the batch** — `renew_batch_credit_amount_basis_bc847570`: "the amount settled
with the customer, less the credit already issued on the agreement, together with the transit settlement
the devices short of the shipment request attract and the allowance a late appraisal attracts, less the
premium standing on the profile's protection cover and the holdback the devices without an erasure
certificate attract, and the figure is rounded to the cent and never falls below nothing."

- Amount settled (tier, `renew_settled_figure_basis_377950d0`): once the revised offer of §4(a) stands,
  "Where one revised offer stands on the agreement's trade-in history the amount settled is that revised
  offer" → **4822.40**.
- Credit already issued (tier, `renew_interim_credit_recovery_97381e91`): the history carries a
  `tradein_credit_issue` of 900.0 and no credit written off, so "the credit already issued on the agreement
  is taken off in full" → **− 900.00**.
- Transit settlement (tier, `renew_transit_shortfall_settlement_acd6ee58`): devices declared on the latest
  shipment request on the agreement = **21**; devices booked in = **18** (`device_count`, "the devices the
  agreement records as having arrived"); 3 short. Value of each device = 6300.00 ÷ 21 = 300.00, below the
  2200.00 transit cover → "the value of each device for each device short" = 300.00 × 3 = **+ 900.00**.
- Late appraisal allowance (tier, `renew_late_appraisal_allowance_949251a5`): booked in `2026-09-04`,
  appraisal recorded `2026-09-15` = 11 calendar days; the programme allows 7 appraisal days and twice that
  is 14; 11 is "more than the programme's appraisal days but no more than twice" → "the delayed appraisal
  allowance of 60.00 USD" → **+ 60.00**.
- Protection premium holdback (tier, `renew_protection_premium_holdback_1ecf4ca7`): a plan standing
  `active` with `premium_outstanding` 240.0 → "the whole premium outstanding is held back" →
  **− 240.00**.
- Erasure certificate holdback (tier, `renew_erasure_certificate_holdback_62aaecf5`): devices booked in 18,
  erasure certificates recorded 6 → 12 without a certificate; `data_wipe_status` `pending` → "the
  uncertified device holdback of 25.00 USD for each device booked in without a certificate" = 25.00 × 12 =
  **− 300.00**.
- 4822.40 − 900.00 + 900.00 + 60.00 − 240.00 − 300.00 = **4342.40 USD**, at the cent, above nothing.

**(c) The last day the credit may be spent.** `renew_batch_settlement_closeout_744bf474`: "The day the
credit expires … falls the Renew programme's credit validity days after the day of issue." Renew Business
Asset Buyback credit "stays spendable" 90 days (`renew_credit_settlement_and_spending_terms_0c4905af`).
`2026-09-18` + 90 days = **`2026-12-17`**.

**(d) The form the credit takes.** A business agreement "is credited by invoice credit or bank transfer
only" (`renew_credit_issue_basis_3d74446a`); the caller asks for "the academy's invoice account rather than
a transfer" → **`business_invoice_credit`**.

**(e) The machines the first wave carries** — `renew_refresh_wave_unit_count_basis_ffc55fa8`: "the machines
the schedule covers, capped at the machines the programme's transit cover will bear, less the machines a
live return authorisation holds back, the machines a recent purchase holds back and the machines the
profile's store account holds back, and the figure is a whole count of machines and never fewer than none."

- Machines the schedule covers: `device_count` **46**. Value of each machine = 9200.00 ÷ 46 = 200.00.
- Transit cover capacity (tier, `renew_refresh_transit_cover_capacity_bc5a30a3`): the cover for Renew Bulk
  IT Refresh Agreement is 2500.00; 200.00 is below it, and the value of the whole schedule, 200.00 × 46 =
  9200.00, is above it → branch 3, "the cover bears the cover divided by the value of each machine, rounded
  down to a whole machine" = 2500.00 ÷ 200.00 = 12.5 → **12 machines**. Cap: min(46, 12) = 12.
- Return holdback (tier, `renew_refresh_return_holdback_1b17e0e7`): "a return authorisation standing
  authorized, and no inspection recorded on the profile's returns within the last twelve months | the
  authorized return figure, 3 machines". `14b45f78-…35aa` stands `authorized`; the only inspection on the
  profile's returns is `2025-05-20`, outside twelve months → **3 machines**.
- Recent purchase holdback (tier, `renew_refresh_recent_purchase_holdback_1ac5ebf2`): the recent purchase
  days are 30; order `6c3db12c-…e94c` was fulfilled `2026-09-05`, 13 days ago, with
  `balance_outstanding` 0.0 → "fulfilled within the recent purchase days and no balance stands outstanding
  on it … the recent order figure, being 2 machines" → **2 machines**.
- Store account holdback (tier, `renew_refresh_store_account_holdback_d1813b4b`): the account stands
  `active` with a balance of 9400.00, above the finance hold balance of 5000.00 → "the part finance figure,
  being 2 machines" → **2 machines**.
- 12 − 3 − 2 − 2 = **5 machines**, a whole count above none.

**(f) The day the wave is asked for**: `2026-10-01`, the day the caller names and will not move.

4. `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool("credit_batch_settlement_af2cb6f5")`; agent calls it with the same
   agreement and customer, `final_credit_amount` **4342.40**, `credit_expiry_date` **`2026-12-17`**,
   `settlement_method` **`business_invoice_credit`**.
5. `unlock_user_discoverable_tool("confirm_refresh_wave_units_923c3678")` and hand it over; the
   **customer** runs it with `tradein_agreement_id` `56ac493d-c42d-48cb-90b5-aa3efd192565`, `customer_id`
   `59d80ff6-ce6f-4a67-992d-f8fba22c6164`, `requested_collection_date` **`2026-10-01`**,
   `units_declared` **5**. Owner: user — B5, "The tool is unlocked for the customer and handed over, and the
   customer themselves runs it, the acceptance and the release being theirs to give."

Forward dependencies: 4 cannot be computed before 3 (the amount settled is the revised offer standing on
the history, and until step 3 none stands); 5 cannot be taken before 4 (§6). Backward: step 3's figure
needs only the buyback agreement, the plan and the dates; step 5's count needs only the schedule, the
returns, the order and the credit account.

Terminal state: the buyback agreement stands `credited`, with 4342.40 credited as invoice credit and
`2026-12-17` as the last spendable day, and a revised-offer entry and a credit entry on its history; the
refresh schedule stands `accepted` with a collection record for 5 machines on `2026-10-01` by freight
collection, consent given by the customer.

#### 6. The problem tree derived from the visible materials alone

**Problems, direction, order.**

- P1 — *put the revised offer the appraisal calls for on the buyback batch's record* (agent act).
- P2 — *close the buyback batch out by crediting the customer* (agent act). Blocked by P1.
- P3 — *accept the refresh schedule and release the machines of its first wave* (customer's own act).
  Blocked by P2. This is the only thing the caller asked for.
- Handling order: P1 → P2 → P3.

**Hop P3 → P2.** Mark: **state-derived**.

1. The thing the caller asked about is governed by `renew_refresh_wave_release_0ae1405f`, whose own rule
   states what the wave count waits on:
   > "**B2. When a wave may be settled.** The machines a wave of the refresh schedule carries are settled
   > only after every batch already appraised on the profile stands credited with the amount owed on it."
   A record-visible state ("stands credited"), with the ordering connective "only after". No tool, no
   policy, no route is named.
2. `find_tradein_agreements` shows the state does not hold: agreement `bf9b906b-…9586` has `status`
   **`appraised`**, `credited_date` "" and `final_credit_amount` "". It is a batch already appraised on
   the profile and it does not stand credited.
3. Searching with the sentence's and the record's own words — "batch", "appraised", "credited", "the amount
   owed" — reaches `renew_batch_settlement_closeout_744bf474`, which describes the write that brings the
   state about in those words: "A batch that has been appraised is closed out by crediting the customer";
   "The agreement is moved to credited with today as the day the credit was issued, the amount credited and
   the last day that credit may be spent written onto it". `renew_credit_issue_basis_3d74446a` confirms the
   state in which credit may be issued ("appraised | yes").
4. The caller never mentions this batch ("He does not ask about the batch first and does not mention it at
   all unless the agent raises it"), so the hop is reached only from B2 plus the agreement record.

**Hop P2 → P1.** Mark: **state-derived**.

1. The close-out document states what the amount waits on:
   > "The amount credited is worked out only after the revised offer the appraisal calls for stands on the
   > agreement's trade-in history."
   Again a record-visible state, again "only after", again no tool or route.
2. `find_tradein_events` on that agreement returns six `tradein_data_wipe_certify` rows and one
   `tradein_credit_issue` row and **no revised-offer row**; so no revised offer stands on the history.
   That the appraisal calls for one is settled by the record itself: `declared_condition` `good` against
   `appraised_condition` `fair`.
3. Searching with the words of the sentence and the record — "revised offer", "trade-in history",
   "appraisal … other than the condition declared" — reaches `renew_revised_offer_entry_82ce6b44`:
   "Where the appraisal of a batch … comes back other than the condition declared, a revised offer is owed
   to the customer"; "One entry is written into the agreement's trade-in history holding the amount the
   offer now stands at, the ground the offer moved on and the condition the appraisal found". That is the
   write that brings the waited-on state about.
4. Nothing further is waited on. `renew_revised_offer_entry_82ce6b44` states no prerequisite, and the state
   its own recording needs (an appraisal on record) already holds. The tree terminates at P1.

No hop is **pre-solved**. Each prerequisite sentence occurs in exactly one document, on the blocked side
(`grep -rl` over `docs/`: "settled only after every batch already appraised" → the wave hub only;
"worked out only after the revised offer" → the close-out hub only). The depended-on documents never say
who waits on them: the close-out document nowhere mentions a wave or a refresh schedule, and the revised
offer document nowhere mentions crediting or a close-out. Each of the five task tool names occurs in
exactly one document, its own hub.

#### 7. Two-way counter-proof

**The conclusion is fully supported.** Every figure in §4 rests on a quoted sentence plus a tool return.

**Closest alternatives, and what excludes each:**

| Closest alternative | What excludes it |
| --- | --- |
| Release 46 machines as the caller asks | the cap: 200.00 each is below the 2500.00 cover while 9200.00 is above it, so the cover bears 2500.00 ÷ 200.00 rounded down = 12 |
| Cap of 1 machine (value each at or above cover) | "A value of each machine standing at exactly the transit cover is at that cover"; 200.00 is below 2500.00 |
| Cap of 46 (whole schedule at or below cover) | 9200.00 is above 2500.00, so the fourth branch does not govern |
| Rounding 12.5 up to 13 | "rounded down to a whole machine" |
| Return holdback of 1 machine | that row needs an authorisation standing `received` **and** an inspection inside twelve months; the authorisation stands `authorized` and the only inspection is `2025-05-20` |
| Return holdback of none | "A profile whose only return authorisation stands in some other state holds none back" — one stands `authorized` |
| Recent purchase holdback of 4 machines | that needs a balance outstanding on the order fulfilled inside 30 days; `balance_outstanding` is 0.0 on the `2026-09-05` order, and the order carrying 11880.0 has no `fulfilled_date` at all |
| Store account holdback of 4 machines | that needs the account standing `delinquent`; it stands `active` with `delinquent_since_date` "" |
| Store account holdback of none | 9400.00 is above the 5000.00 finance hold balance; "A balance standing at exactly 5000.00 USD is not above" |
| Revised offer at 5100.00 (the appraisal) | the gap of 1200.00 is no more than twice the 630.00 tolerance, so the half-gap branch governs, not the third |
| Revised offer at 6300.00 (quote honoured) | the gap of 1200.00 is more than the 630.00 tolerance, so the first branch does not govern |
| Cover deduction of 90.00 | that row needs the plan standing "in claim hold"; it stands `active` |
| Cover deduction of nothing | the third row covers "cover on it that may be transferred"; `transferable_flag` is False |
| Ageing counted from the day the batch was booked in | that branch needs the batch booked in **within** the quote validity days; `2026-08-20`→`2026-09-04` is 15 days against 14 |
| No ageing markdown / 6 per cent | 29 days is more than 21, and six erasure certificates stand recorded; "An offer that has aged exactly 21 days has not aged more than 21 days" fixes the boundary the other way |
| Amount settled = 5100.00 | once one revised offer stands, "that one is settled whether it is higher or lower than the amount the appraisal supports" |
| Nothing taken off for credit already issued | the history carries `tradein_credit_issue` 900.0 and no write-off, so it is "taken off in full" |
| Transit settlement of nothing, or on 18 declared | the request declares 21 and 18 were booked in; the value of each device is the quote over the **devices the request declared** |
| Late appraisal allowance of 140.00 | 11 days is "no more than twice the programme's appraisal days" (14) |
| Erasure holdback at 8.00 each | that row needs the data standing "verified by the retailer"; `data_wipe_status` is `pending` |
| Premium holdback of half | that needs the plan standing in claim hold; it stands `active` |
| Credit as `bank_transfer` | the caller asks for the invoice account "rather than a transfer" |
| Wave day moved | the caller refuses to move `2026-10-01`, and nothing in the corpus requires another day |

**Wrong answer "do only the one thing the customer asked for".** He asked only for the wave. Releasing it
alone is excluded by B2 of the release document read against the agreement record: the machines of a wave
"are settled only after every batch already appraised on the profile stands credited with the amount owed
on it", and `bf9b906b-…9586` stands `appraised` with no credited date — so the count could not lawfully be
settled and the release would leave the schedule accepted on a count the rule does not allow. Crediting it
is in turn excluded until the revised offer stands, by the close-out document's own sentence against an
event history that carries no revised offer. Both exclusions come from prerequisite sentences on the
blocked side plus records; neither from a pointer, a tool name or a route.

**Fall-back answers, from each computation document and the records alone.**

- Revised offer, on `renew_revised_offer_amount_basis_e684148d` alone: "a revised offer … is put at the
  amount the appraisal supports, rounded to the cent", with the worked steps taking nothing off as a cover
  deduction and applying no ageing markdown → **5100.00 USD**. Definite, different from 4822.40.
- Amount credited, on `renew_batch_credit_amount_basis_bc847570` alone: "The amount settled is the amount
  the appraisal supports, the credit already issued on the agreement is nothing, and no transit settlement,
  no late appraisal allowance, no protection premium and no erasure holdback are counted" → **5100.00

**The formerly-latent day-count conflict, re-derived — this is the one that was materially load-bearing.**
Round 1 recorded as a policy-side note (K5) that `tradein_appraisal_grading` defined the appraisal window in
**business** days while the factors measuring against that same figure measured in **calendar** days. I have
now computed both readings on this task's own dates: `device_received_date` `2026-09-04` is a Friday and
`appraised_date` `2026-09-15` is a Tuesday, which is **11 calendar days** but **exactly 7 business days** —
and Renew Business Asset Buyback allows the appraisal 7 days. So the business-day reading put the appraisal
*within* the programme's appraisal days and added **nothing**, while the calendar reading put it above them
and added the delayed appraisal allowance of **60.00**. The conflict was live, sat exactly on the threshold,
and was worth 60.00 on the credited amount.

It is now closed on the visible surface, in two places I checked separately:
- `renew_bench_appraisal_basis_42b4f455` registers the retirement verbatim — "Within that clause the words
  *counted in business days from the day the device was booked in* are **no longer in force**, and how the
  days of an appraisal are counted is settled on the current basis for the Renew programme concerned; the
  appraisal days the programme publishes stand as a published figure";
- `renew_late_appraisal_allowance_949251a5` now states the convention outright — "counted in calendar days
  from the day the batch was booked in to the day the appraisal was recorded, **and the programme's appraisal
  days are read against that calendar count**" — and `renew_offer_ageing_anchor_648d82c9` carries the same
  sentence for its own span.

`business days` now occurs in exactly one `tradein` document and only inside that retired quotation
(`grep -rl` over `docs/`). 11 calendar days is more than 7 and no more than 14, so **60.00** stands and the
credited amount is 4342.40 on an unambiguous basis. **K5 is closed.** (The ageing anchor was never at risk:
its first branch already governs, the batch having been booked in 15 days after a 14-day quote.)

**Fall-backs, re-run.** All three of this task's computation documents still yield a definite number
differing from the full-corpus answer: the revised offer gives **5100.00**, the amount credited gives
**5100.00**, and the wave gives **46**, against 4822.40, 4342.40 and 5. The batch-credit computation
document has been rewritten — the "Amounts named in this basis" block is gone, `meta.carries` is `[]`, and
its worked figure now runs on 3275.00 over 9 devices — so a reader of it alone learns the defaults and
nothing else. No computation document prints its own task's fall-back.

**Verdict unchanged: PASS (no `KB-RUNTIME RED`)** — and now resting on a visible surface that settles the
one convention which, in round 1, the documents left the reader to guess at on a figure that mattered.
